/*
# SimpleLayout — stack children along an axis

The stacking idiom: siblings placed one after another along
`axis`, in child order, `spacing` apart (negative overlaps). The cross axis
and all sizes stay the children's own — a child centers itself across a row
with the ordinary `y = center`. Invisible children are skipped and their
space reclaimed; a skipped child still gets the slot it would occupy, so
re-showing it needs no special case. A `Spacer` child flexes to absorb the
run's slack along the axis (between two groups it pushes them apart; one on
each side centers the run).

Written in Declare over the Layout kernel: the whole strategy is this one
pure place() — one box per laid child, aligned by index.

```declare
col: View [ x = 20, y = 20,
    layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = y, spacing = 8 ],
    View [ width = 160, height = 24, cornerRadius = 6, fill = steelblue ],
    View [ width = 120, height = 24, cornerRadius = 6, fill = cadetblue ],
    View [ width = 190, height = 24, cornerRadius = 6, fill = slategray ]
    ]
```

## axis
Which way children stack: `y` (the default) or `x`. **A bare literal, not a string** —
`axis = x`, and note that `x` here is the axis token, not the position attribute.

## spacing
The gap between adjacent children. **Negative overlaps them**, which is how a stack of
cards or avatars is built.

## place()
The whole strategy: one box per laid child, positioned along the axis in child order.
**The cross axis and every size stay the children's own** — a child centres itself
across a row with the ordinary `y = center`. Override it in a subclass for custom
geometry; a `Layout`'s `place()` **may** aggregate over children, which is the one place
that is allowed.
*/

class SimpleLayout extends Layout [
    axis: Axis = y,
    spacing: number = 0,

    place() {
        const axis = this.axis
        const size = axis == "x" ? "width" : "height"
        const kids = this.laid()
        const flexing = (c) => (c).flexes === true

        // slack, only when someone flexes: the view's extent along the axis
        // minus the rigid content and the gaps between visible children
        // a child's slot is its FOOTPRINT (the scale/rotation-composed box),
        // so a scale = 0.5 child occupies half the run and a rotated card
        // reserves what it visibly covers; the box's lead compensates the
        // transform's own offset so the VISIBLE edge lands on the slot
        let each = 0
        let flexN = 0
        for (const c of kids) if (c.visible && flexing(c)) flexN = flexN + 1
        if (flexN > 0) {
            let content = 0
            let visN = 0
            for (const c of kids) {
                if (!c.visible) continue
                visN = visN + 1
                if (!flexing(c)) content = content + (c).footprint()[size]
            }
            const extent = this.view == null ? 0 : (this.view)[size]
            each = Math.max(0, (extent - content - this.spacing * Math.max(0, visN - 1)) / flexN)
        }

        let pos = 0
        return kids.map((c) => {
            const flex = c.visible && flexing(c)
            // footprint, never bounds: the strategy must not read the slot it
            // writes (one-pass discipline). A flexing child's size is ALLOCATED
            // (box.w/h), so its footprint is never consulted — lead 0, raw slot.
            const f = flex ? null : (c).footprint()
            const lead = f == null ? 0 : (axis == "x" ? f.x : f.y)
            const box = (axis == "x" ? ({ x: pos - lead }) : ({ y: pos - lead }))
            if (flex) box[axis == "x" ? "w" : "h"] = each
            if (c.visible) pos = pos + (flex ? each : (f)[size]) + this.spacing
            return box
            })
        }
    ]

/*
# Icon — the drawn mark

A small monochrome mark, **drawn** rather than typed. Fonts are not UI objects:
their glyphs are not guaranteed to be present, they rasterize differently on
every platform, and the ones that exist are the wrong shapes — a `✓` sits on the
text baseline and reads like a square-root sign, not like a checkmark. The house
already knew this in three places before it had a name for it (`Checkbox.mark`,
`Menu.check`, `Combobox.disc` are all drawn); this is that decision, stated once.

### Writing one

Subclass and override `draw`. Author the shape in a **16×16 box** — `unit`
converts it to whatever size the host asked for:

```declare-fragment
class SparkIcon extends Icon [
    draw(d: Draw) {
        d.scale(unit, unit)
        d.strokeStyle = ink; d.lineWidth = weight / unit
        d.beginPath(); d.moveTo(8, 1); d.lineTo(8, 15); d.stroke()
        }
    ]
```

Overriding a **method** is the refinement path that works — re-opening an
inherited child is not (`cap:` on a `Button` subclass fails at instantiate), so
the shape lives in `draw` and everything adjustable is a slot.

### Size changes the drawing, not the shape

Every icon is ONE path. There are no per-size variants, no thresholds, nothing
redrawn at a breakpoint: `unit` scales the 16-box to whatever the host asked for,
so a 64px icon is the 16px icon at 4×, exactly.

The **stroke** is the deliberate exception. `d.lineWidth = weight / unit` sits
*inside* `d.scale(unit, unit)`, so the two cancel and the line lands at a constant
`weight` in **device pixels at every size**. An icon's line therefore matches the
1px rules and text weights it sits among, instead of fattening as it grows.

The cost is that the stroke-to-size ratio falls: 1.6px is 10% of a 16px icon, 5%
at 32, 2.5% at 64. Across 14–18px, which is every site in this corpus, that is
invisible. Past ~32 an icon starts reading as a fine-line drawing rather than a
mark — so **this set is built for chrome sizes**, and a large display icon (an
empty-state mark, an about-box graphic) would want the opposite: `d.lineWidth =
weight` *outside* the scale, so the line grows with the drawing. Real icon
systems take a third road and redraw per optical size range; that is a bigger
undertaking than this set needs.

`test/probe/iconbook.declare` shows the ramp — the same chevron and bulb at 16,
24, 32, 48 and 64 — if the tradeoff ever needs re-judging.

### What is NOT an Icon

Application art. The desktop's dock icons are the case to look at before
reaching for this class: they rest at 56px and grow under the magnification
swell, they are polychrome (`gradient(hue1, hue2)` behind a hue-parameterised
drawing), and their **width animates every frame**. Each of those alone rules
them out — the constant stroke that suits a 16px mark is 2.9% of a 56px one and
reads spindly; `ink` is a single colour; and an animated width is the one thing
this set forbids.

The line is not "drawn versus not drawn" — dock art is drawn too. It is
**chrome vocabulary versus identity**. A mark that says *close*, *expand*,
*checked*, *this is the dark theme* belongs here, at a size the host states.
A mark that says *this is Calendar* does not, and belongs to the app that owns
the identity.

Desktop has both, which is what makes it the clarifying example: its menu rows
take `WindowIcon` and `CodeIcon` from this set, while its dock keeps `DockIcon`.

### Two rules

**Scale inside the body, never with the View's `scale`.** A recording rasterizes
into a canvas sized to its own ink bounds at device resolution
(`dom-backend.ts` `rasterize()`), while `scale` is a CSS transform applied
*after* — so `scale = { width / 16 }` would rasterize 16 pixels and stretch them.
Crisp at exactly 16, soft at every other size, which is most of them. Scaling
inside the recording allocates the raster at true size instead.

**Never animate an icon's `width`.** Reading size inside `draw` makes the
recording size-dependent: an animated size re-records AND reallocates the backing
canvas every frame, which is what dragged the dock's magnification from 60 to
~25fps (`adaptive-draw-cache.md`). A static size re-records once and costs
nothing after. Measured: 120 icons re-recording their *content* every frame runs
frame-bound at 16.6ms, cheaper than the 120 text glyphs they replace.

Colour is not a rule — `ink` follows the prevailing text colour, so an icon beside
a muted label goes muted on its own, and a host that needs a different ink (a
menu row's check inverting on the hot row) simply sets it.

## ink
The mark's colour. Follows the **prevailing `textColor`**, so an icon beside a muted
label goes muted on its own. **The trap: that slot falls back to black platform-wide**,
so an icon in a context that never states a text colour renders black and vanishes on a
dark surface. State `ink` unless you know the context sets one — `IconHost` does it for
every icon built by name.

## weight
Stroke width in **final device pixels, not authored ones**. Divide by `unit` inside
`draw` (`d.lineWidth = weight / unit`) and the scale cancels, so the line lands at a
constant weight at every size and matches the 1px rules and text it sits among.

## unit
The 16-box-to-host-size scale factor. **Multiply the path by it; divide the stroke by
it.** Every icon is one path at one size, scaled — there are no per-size variants.

## isIcon
**Internal.** The marker a layout keys on to place an icon without knowing which shape
it is — not API.
*/

/*
# IconHost — a named icon, materialized

   A control names its icon (`iconLeft = TrashIcon`) rather than nesting one,
   because a control is a leaf and everything else about it is an attribute — and
   because an attribute is the one form where AUTHORED and BOUND are the same
   mechanism. `IconHost` is what turns that name into a live view, through the
   same `app.createView` seam the menu's `iconKind` already uses.

   It reserves no space when empty, so a control's `contentWidth` measures only
   the slots that are actually filled and an icon-less button needs no special
   case.

   LIMITATION, deliberate for now: the name is consumed once, at construction.
   A control whose icon must CHANGE at runtime (a play/pause toggle) is not
   served by this yet — that needs a name-valued slot the runtime re-materializes
   on change, which is a runtime feature, not a library one. Every site in this
   corpus names its icon statically.

## kind
The icon **class name** to build (`"TrashIcon"`). `""` builds nothing and the host
collapses to zero width, so an icon-less control needs no special case. **Consumed once,
at construction** — assigning a new name later does not re-materialize the icon. A name
that is only ever computed needs `use [ Name ]` to survive the build.

## ink
The colour handed to the icon this host builds. **`createView` cannot pass attributes,
so a prevailing slot is the only channel that reaches it** — this publishes `textColor`
for exactly that. Defaults to `theme.text` rather than the platform's inherited black,
which is what stops a host-built icon from rendering invisibly on a dark surface.

## onInit
Builds the named icon. Fires once.
*/

class IconHost extends View [
    kind: string = "",
    width  = { classroot.kind == "" ? 0 : this.iconSize },
    height = { this.iconSize },
    y = center,
    visible = { classroot.kind != "" },

    // THE INK CHANNEL. `createView` cannot pass attributes, so the only way to
    // reach the icon it builds is a PREVAILING slot — and the one `Icon.ink`
    // reads is `textColor`. Publishing it here is what lets a host state its
    // ink at all.
    //
    // The default matters more than it looks: prevailing `textColor` falls back
    // to 0x000000 platform-wide, so an icon that inherited it rendered BLACK —
    // fine on a light surface by luck, invisible on a dark one. Every
    // host-created icon in the corpus was doing that. `theme.text` is a floor
    // that is never invisible in either palette.

    ink: Color = { this.theme.text },
    textColor = { classroot.ink },

    onInit() { if (this.kind != "") this.createView(this.kind, ({ })) }
    ]


class Icon extends View [
    // The marker a layout keys on, so a control can place its icon without
    // caring which shape it is (the Segment/Segmented discipline).

    isIcon: boolean = true,

    // Size comes from the CONTEXT: `iconSize` is prevailing, so a menu states 16
    // once and every icon in every row answers. A use site may override it.

    width  = { this.iconSize },
    height = { this.width },
    y = center,

    // Follows the PREVAILING text colour, so an icon beside a muted label goes
    // muted on its own. The trap: that slot falls back to 0x000000 platform-wide,
    // so an icon in a context which never states a text colour renders BLACK and
    // disappears on a dark surface. State `ink` unless you know the context sets
    // one — `IconHost` does it for every icon built by name.

    ink: Color = { this.textColor },
    weight: number = 1.6,        // stroke width in FINAL pixels, not authored ones

    // 16-box → host size. Multiply the path by this; divide the stroke by it, so
    // the line keeps its true weight instead of scaling with the drawing.

    unit: number = { this.width / 16 }
    ]

/*
# Core icons

The marks the chrome uses everywhere: a chevron, a check, a close, plus/minus,
and the menu's help bulb. Each is authored in a 16×16 box and scaled to the
host's `iconSize` inside its recording (see `icon.declare`).

Geometry is a property of the SET, not of the site: one stroke weight, round caps
and joins throughout, one path per shape. Before this, the corpus drew a
checkmark two ways (stroke 2.5 mitered in `Checkbox`, 1.8 round in `Menu`) and a
chevron at least six, three of them inside the library. Ink stays local — a menu
row inverts its check on the hot row, a checkbox always uses `accentText`.
*/



/*
# ChevronIcon

The **disclosure** mark: a menu drops, a pane opens, a select expands. Every
disclosure in the chrome is this one class turned by its `dir`, which is what makes
them agree. For a direction that is itself the state — a sort order, a trend — reach
for `ArrowIcon` instead; the two must not look alike.

## dir
The resting orientation: `"down"` (the default), `"up"`, `"left"` or `"right"`. Sugar
over `angle`.

## angle
The rotation in radians, and **the primitive, so it can be sprung** — an `Accordion`
twisty turns in step with its pane sliding open rather than snapping between two
states. The turn lives in the recording deliberately: the mark rotates inside its
16-box while the box stays put. (The View-level `rotation` attribute turns the whole
box — the wrong tool for a glyph whose frame should not move.)

## draw()
Renders the chevron. Override to replace the mark while keeping the class's role.
*/

class ChevronIcon extends Icon [
    dir: string = "down",                       // down | up | left | right
    angle: number = { classroot.dir == "up" ? Math.PI
                    : classroot.dir == "left" ? Math.PI / 2
                    : classroot.dir == "right" ? -Math.PI / 2 : 0 },

    draw(d: Draw) {
        d.scale(this.unit, this.unit)
        d.strokeStyle = this.ink
        d.lineWidth = this.weight / this.unit
        d.lineCap = "round"
        d.lineJoin = "round"
        d.save()
        d.translate(8, 8)
        d.rotate(this.angle)
        d.beginPath()
        d.moveTo(-3.5, -1.75)
        d.lineTo(0, 1.75)
        d.lineTo(3.5, -1.75)
        d.stroke()
        d.restore()
        }
    ]


/*
# ArrowIcon

An arrow, **not a chevron** — the two mean different things and must not look alike.
A chevron *discloses*; an arrow points at a direction that **is itself the state**:
sort ascending, a trend, a transfer. The shaft is what a chevron lacks. Tracker had
the two adjacent — a sort-direction control beside a sort-menu popper — and one shape
for both read as a mistake.

## dir
Which way it points: `"up"` (the default), `"down"`, `"left"` or `"right"`.

## angle
The rotation in radians, sprungable like `ChevronIcon`'s.

## draw()
Renders the arrow.
*/

class ArrowIcon extends Icon [
    dir: string = "up",                         // up | down | left | right
    angle: number = { classroot.dir == "down" ? Math.PI
                    : classroot.dir == "left" ? -Math.PI / 2
                    : classroot.dir == "right" ? Math.PI / 2 : 0 },

    draw(d: Draw) {
        d.scale(this.unit, this.unit)
        d.strokeStyle = this.ink
        d.lineWidth = this.weight / this.unit
        d.lineCap = "round"
        d.lineJoin = "round"
        d.save()
        d.translate(8, 8)
        d.rotate(this.angle)
        d.beginPath()
        d.moveTo(0, 5.2); d.lineTo(0, -5.2)     // the shaft is what a chevron lacks
        d.moveTo(-3.6, -1.6); d.lineTo(0, -5.2); d.lineTo(3.6, -1.6)
        d.stroke()
        d.restore()
        }
    ]


/*
# CheckIcon

The tick — a checked menu row, a `Checkbox`'s mark, a confirmation. **Ink stays
local**: a menu row inverts its check on the highlighted row while a checkbox always
uses the accent text colour, so the host sets `ink` rather than the icon assuming it.

## draw()
Renders the tick. Before this class the corpus drew a checkmark two ways — stroke 2.5
mitered in `Checkbox`, 1.8 round in `Menu` — which is the drift one shape ends.
*/

class CheckIcon extends Icon [
    draw(d: Draw) {
        d.scale(this.unit, this.unit)
        d.strokeStyle = this.ink
        d.lineWidth = this.weight / this.unit
        d.lineCap = "round"
        d.lineJoin = "round"
        d.beginPath()
        d.moveTo(3, 8.5)
        d.lineTo(6.5, 12)
        d.lineTo(13, 4.5)
        d.stroke()
        }
    ]


/*
# CloseIcon

The dismiss mark: a window close box, a chip's remove affordance, a dialog's corner.

## draw()
Renders the cross.
*/

class CloseIcon extends Icon [
    draw(d: Draw) {
        d.scale(this.unit, this.unit)
        d.strokeStyle = this.ink
        d.lineWidth = this.weight / this.unit
        d.lineCap = "round"
        d.beginPath()
        d.moveTo(4.5, 4.5); d.lineTo(11.5, 11.5)
        d.moveTo(11.5, 4.5); d.lineTo(4.5, 11.5)
        d.stroke()
        }
    ]


/*
# PlusIcon

Add. Pairs with `MinusIcon` at the same stroke and cap, so a stepper's two ends match.

## draw()
Renders the plus.
*/

class PlusIcon extends Icon [
    draw(d: Draw) {
        d.scale(this.unit, this.unit)
        d.strokeStyle = this.ink
        d.lineWidth = this.weight / this.unit
        d.lineCap = "round"
        d.beginPath()
        d.moveTo(8, 3.5); d.lineTo(8, 12.5)
        d.moveTo(3.5, 8); d.lineTo(12.5, 8)
        d.stroke()
        }
    ]


/*
# MinusIcon

Remove, and the partially-checked state of a tri-state box. Pairs with `PlusIcon`.

## draw()
Renders the bar.
*/

class MinusIcon extends Icon [
    draw(d: Draw) {
        d.scale(this.unit, this.unit)
        d.strokeStyle = this.ink
        d.lineWidth = this.weight / this.unit
        d.lineCap = "round"
        d.beginPath()
        d.moveTo(3.5, 8); d.lineTo(12.5, 8)
        d.stroke()
        }
    ]


/*
# LightbulbIcon

The help affordance — the one FILLED mark in a stroked set: a continuous
teardrop of glass over a three-bar tapering base.

## draw()
Renders the bulb. **This one mark is filled, and does not answer to `weight`**
— the contour carries its weight in the outline itself, so there is no stroke
to widen. The bulb keeps its own visual weight at every rung.
*/

// The one filled mark: the CONTOUR is the drawing — glass as a continuous
// teardrop, the base as three tapering bars — so `weight` has no stroke to
// act on here. No y-flip anywhere: the path counts DOWN, like this canvas.

class LightbulbIcon extends Icon [
    draw(d: Draw) {
        d.scale(this.unit, this.unit)
        d.fillStyle = this.ink
        d.beginPath()
        d.moveTo(3.4, 4.235)
        d.bezierCurveTo(3.4, 6.876, 4.982, 7.529, 5.422, 12.115)
        d.bezierCurveTo(5.449, 12.363, 5.587, 12.521, 5.848, 12.521)
        d.lineTo(10.152, 12.521)
        d.bezierCurveTo(10.42, 12.521, 10.558, 12.363, 10.585, 12.115)
        d.bezierCurveTo(11.025, 7.529, 12.6, 6.876, 12.6, 4.235)
        d.bezierCurveTo(12.6, 1.863, 10.572, 0.0, 8.0, 0.0)
        d.bezierCurveTo(5.428, 0.0, 3.4, 1.863, 3.4, 4.235)
        d.closePath()
        d.moveTo(4.438, 4.235)
        d.bezierCurveTo(4.438, 2.379, 6.068, 1.038, 8.0, 1.038)
        d.bezierCurveTo(9.932, 1.038, 11.562, 2.379, 11.562, 4.235)
        d.bezierCurveTo(11.562, 6.209, 10.255, 6.676, 9.636, 11.483)
        d.lineTo(6.37, 11.483)
        d.bezierCurveTo(5.745, 6.676, 4.438, 6.209, 4.438, 4.235)
        d.closePath()
        d.moveTo(5.827, 14.006)
        d.lineTo(10.18, 14.006)
        d.bezierCurveTo(10.407, 14.006, 10.578, 13.827, 10.578, 13.6)
        d.bezierCurveTo(10.578, 13.38, 10.407, 13.202, 10.18, 13.202)
        d.lineTo(5.827, 13.202)
        d.bezierCurveTo(5.6, 13.202, 5.422, 13.38, 5.422, 13.6)
        d.bezierCurveTo(5.422, 13.827, 5.6, 14.006, 5.827, 14.006)
        d.closePath()
        d.moveTo(8.0, 16.0)
        d.bezierCurveTo(9.066, 16.0, 9.953, 15.477, 10.021, 14.687)
        d.lineTo(5.985, 14.687)
        d.bezierCurveTo(6.034, 15.477, 6.927, 16.0, 8.0, 16.0)
        d.closePath()
        d.fill()
        }
    ]

/*
# Menu

The record-driven menu (planes.md §4–§6): items are DATA — the component
arranges; the author never composes rows. The standard record covers real OS
menus:

    { id, label, key?, icon?, enabled?, checked?, divider?, submenu?, kind?, props? }

- `key` renders right-aligned (display only — registration is the Keys
  service's, later).
- `icon: "ClassName"` names an icon class for the leading column, and the label
  shifts right to make room — the same vocabulary `Segmented`'s choices use.

  This was THREE mechanisms before the icon set landed: a text glyph (`"◐"`), a
  hardcoded `"lightbulb"` that special-cased its way to a drawn bulb because no
  glyph matched, and `iconKind` naming a class. The middle one was the tell —
  somebody needed a mark the fonts could not give, and the escape hatch already
  existed. One field now; a COMPUTED name needs its class kept with
  `use [ Name ]`, since no static reference reaches it.
- `enabled: false` dims the row (theme.disabledOpacity) and refuses pick.
- `{ divider: true }` is a separator line.
- `submenu: [ …records… ]` marks a cascade (the ▸ arrow; the cascade itself
  lands with the roving-keyboard stage).
- `kind: "ClassName"` renders the row's CONTENT with a named author class
  (app.createView — keep data-only classes with `use [ Name ]`), passed
  `props` as its datapath context. Behavior stays the row's: highlight,
  pick, keyboard are the menu's, always.

Declared ONCE, opened by many (the worked example): rows carry
`onContextMenu(e) { app.rowMenu.openAt(this, e) }`; the menu's `items`
constraint derives from `opener` — per-row variation with zero per-row
instances, live while open. `openAt` point-positions (the context-menu
rule); `openFor` drops below a control (the attached-menu rule); both
RAISE the menu (promotion — order is a slot) and clamp inside the app.

Dismissal: the BACKDROP (a full-app child under the panel) — a press
outside closes AND is swallowed, the Mac rule (planes.md §12.1, resolved
for v1); Escape closes; pick closes after delivery.

```declare
App [ width = 320, height = 130,
    chose: string = "",
    edit: Menu [ items = { [ ({ id: "cut", label: "Cut", key: "⌘X" }),
                            ({ id: "copy", label: "Copy", key: "⌘C", checked: true }),
                            ({ divider: true }),
                            ({ id: "paste", label: "Paste", enabled: false }) ] },
        picked(id: string) { app.chose = id }
        ],
    Button [ x = 20, y = 20, label = "Edit", menu = { app.edit } ],
    Text [ x = 20, y = 74, text = { app.chose == "" ? "nothing picked" : "picked: " + app.chose } ]
    ]
```

## items
The rows, as **records — never children**. A menu arranges its own rows, so handing it
views is not merely discouraged, there is nowhere to put them. The record is
`{ id, label, key?, icon?, enabled?, checked?, divider?, submenu?, kind?, props? }`;
a plain array is fine (no `Dataset` required). Because it is an ordinary attribute it
can be a constraint — **derive it from `opener` and one menu serves every row of a
table**, live while it is open.

## opener
The view this menu was opened for, set by `openAt`/`openFor` and cleared on close.
**The key to declaring one menu and opening it from many places**: read it in the
`items` constraint to vary the rows per opener, with no per-opener instance.

## shown
Whether the menu is up. Read it; **open through `openAt`/`openFor` rather than
assigning it**, or the menu appears unplaced, unraised, and without its keyboard claim.
Closing by assignment skips the cascade teardown for the same reason.

## picked()
**The delivery seam — override it at the use site.** Receives the picked row's `id`,
and the id is the whole message. Called *after* the menu has left the screen, so a slow
action can never freeze an open menu.

## openFor()
Opens the menu **anchored below a control**, flipping above it when there is not room
below and more room above — the native select discipline. The attached-menu rule; what
`Control.menu` uses.

## openAt()
Opens the menu **at the pointer**, given the serving view and the pointer event — the
context-menu rule. Clamped inside the app like any placement. `ContextMenu` wraps this
as `open`.

## close()
Takes the menu down, closes any cascade under it, and releases the keyboard claim.

## pick()
Delivers a row: **dismisses first, then delivers**, one painted frame later — the
native menu contract, and the reason a long-running action cannot leave a menu stranded
on screen. A submenu routes to the root so the whole chain closes as one.

## activeRow

# MenuBar

The record-driven menu bar (planes.md §4–§6): whole menus are DATA —

    menus = { [ ({ id, label, bold?, items: [ …menu records… ] }), … ] }

— and the component arranges. ONE internal Menu serves every title; its
`items` constraint derives from the open title's record, so item state
(enabled, checked, labels) stays LIVE while the menu is up. Because the
records are the single declaration, an app can derive its key registry
from the same array the bar renders — nothing is declared twice (the
Newton keys direction, proven in apps/desktop).

Tracking is the classic desktop behavior: titles do NOT highlight on mere hover;
a click opens (and highlights) a title; while any menu is open, moving
across another title switches to it; clicking the open title closes.

Delivery is the one seam: `picked(id)` — override at the use site.

```declare

    bar: MenuBar [ x = 12, y = 8,
        menus = { [ ({ id: "file", label: "File", items: [ ({ id: "new", label: "New", key: "⌘N" }),
                                                          ({ id: "open", label: "Open…" }) ] }),
                    ({ id: "edit", label: "Edit", items: [ ({ id: "undo", label: "Undo" }),
                                                           ({ divider: true }),
                                                           ({ id: "cut", label: "Cut" }) ] }) ] },
        picked(id: string) { app.chose = id }
        ],
    Text [ x = 20, y = 70, text = { app.chose == "" ? "nothing picked" : "picked: " + app.chose } ]
    ]
```

The whole bar as **data**: `[ { id, label, bold?, kind?, items: [ …menu records… ] } ]`,
where `items` is exactly `Menu`'s record shape. **One internal `Menu` serves every
title**, deriving its rows from the open one — so item state stays live while a menu is
up, and there is nothing to keep in step. Because the records are the single
declaration, an app can derive its keyboard-shortcut registry from the same array the
bar renders.

## picked()
**The delivery seam — override it at the use site.** Receives the picked item's `id`
from any menu in the bar; the id is the whole message.

## ink
Overrides the *titles'* colour, for a bar drawn straight over a wallpaper where the
platform text turns light. `null` uses the theme's text colour. **The dropdown menus
stay themed either way** — this is the bar's own ink, not the menu's.

## openId
Which title's menu is open, by id — `""` when none is.

## shown
Whether any menu in the bar is currently open.

## openMenu()
Opens a title's menu and keeps the bar itself above the menu's backdrop, which is what
lets tracking continue while a menu is up.

## trackMenu()
Switches to another title while a menu is already open — **bar tracking**: titles do
not highlight on mere hover, but once a menu is open, crossing another title opens that
one.

## stepMenu()

open menu when a submenu is up or the rover sits on one.

than from a stale perch.

## placed
Whether the ring has ever had a target to park on. **The first appearance never flies**,
because a flight from nowhere is a streak across the app.

## ringRole()
The theme's election, from `theme.focusRing`: `"both"` (the default), `"travel"`
(flight plus the OpenLaszlo idle fade), `"rest"` (appears in place and stays, no
flight), or `"off"`. **`"off"` is legitimate only when the theme's own controls carry
an at-rest focus indication** — the invariant belongs to the theme-and-components pair,
not to the ring alone.

## restRole()
Whether the elected role includes resting — a resting ring does not idle-fade.

## travelRole()
Whether the elected role includes the flight.

## snapTo()
Lands the ring on its target immediately, skipping the flight. What a pointer focus, a
first appearance, and `theme.focusAnimate = false` all use — **and what a target moving
under a resting ring uses**, so a dragged slider thumb carries the ring rigidly instead
of springing after it.

## overlayUp
True while an overlay owns the keyboard (an open `Menu`). **The ring stands down** —
the menu's own rover is the focus story, and a page ring poking around a panel reads as
chrome fighting chrome.

## idle
True once a travel-role ring has sat still long enough to fade out — the OpenLaszlo
idle behaviour. A resting ring never sets it.

## draw()
Renders the outline: four corner arcs with arms whose length is a pure function of
distance from the target, so the physics does the choreography. Override to replace the
rendition entirely. `theme.focusSights = true` restores the open-bracket "target
sights" reading; `theme.focusRingInnerWidth` adds the Fluent two-tone band.

## tx
**Internal.** The target x the springs chase.

## ty
**Internal.** The target y.

## tw
**Internal.** The target width.

## th
**Internal.** The target height.

## trad
**Internal.** The target corner radius — the silhouette reshapes as the ring travels.

## rad
**Internal.** The ring's current corner radius, sprung toward `trad`.

## gen
**Internal.** The idle-fade generation counter, so a retarget cancels the pending fade.

class FocusRing extends View [ opacity = 0,

    // an OVERLAY owns the keys (an open menu — Keys.navClaim): the ring
    // stands down while it's up — the menu's rover is the focus story, and
    // a page ring poking around a panel reads as chrome fighting chrome

    overlayUp: boolean = false,
    claims: Keys [ onNavClaim(on: boolean) { classroot.overlayUp = on }
        ],

    // where the ring is HEADED — written by the subscription; the springs chase

    tx: number = 0,
    ty: number = 0,
    tw: number = 0,
    th: number = 0,
    trad: number = 8,
    rad: number = 8,
    shown: boolean = false,
    placed: boolean = false,                     // has the ring EVER had a target to park on?

    // the OL idle fade — TRAVEL role only; a resting ring does not fade

    idle: boolean = false,
    gen:  number = 0,

    // role helpers over the theme election

    ringRole()  { const r = this.theme.focusRing; return r == false ? "off" : r == true || r == null ? "both" : r },
    restRole()  { const r = this.ringRole(); return r == "both" || r == "rest" },
    travelRole() { const r = this.ringRole(); return r == "both" || r == "travel" },

    snapTo() { this.x = this.tx; this.y = this.ty; this.width = this.tw; this.height = this.th; this.rad = this.trad },

    // tracked through the parent chain and focusShape(), so an arrow-keyed
    // slider thumb (or a reflowing layout) moves the resting ring with it.
    // The band sits OUTSIDE the silhouette: inner edge touching the control's
    // boundary (the Mac halo's hug), displaced by gap + half the stroke.

    focus: Focus [
        onGeometry(g: FocusGeometry) {
            if (g.root != this.root) return
            // TRAVEL WITH the target's scroller: the ring's surface re-hosts
            // inside the scrolled container and positions in ITS content
            // coordinates — the platform then carries ring and control
            // together, zero lag, no per-scroll re-derive (the sticky-frame
            // inverse). A backend without the ride keeps root-space reactive
            // positioning.

            const prevHome = (this)._lastHome

            const py = classroot.y
            const homed = classroot.travelWith(g.scroller)

            const gy = homed ? g.homeY : g.y
            // Crossing scroll HOMES (the bar's button → a control in the
            // scrolled page): the flight must still fly. The ring's current
            // position converts through ROOT space into the DESTINATION
            // home's coordinates — same painted spot, new numbers — and the
            // springs then travel entirely within the new space (correct
            // even if that pane scrolls mid-flight).

                    ? ({ x: px, y: py })
                    : (() => { const o = prevHome.rootOrigin(); return ({ x: o.x + px - prevHome.scrollX, y: o.y + py - prevHome.scrollY }) })()

            // any ancestor transform above the scroller reaches its surface
            // through the platform, so frame-space extents would double-apply it

            // ring — a dragged slider thumb, a reflow — takes the ring with it
            // rigidly: the springs' targets just moved, so land them NOW. The
            // discriminator is target IDENTITY (a handler-scratch expando — not
            // reactive state, just the previous event's view for comparison).
            ;(this)._lastTarget = g.view

            if (!Focus.byKeyboard()) { classroot.shown = false; classroot.snapTo(); classroot.placed = true; return }

            // the flourish, or the role is rest-only (appear in place, stay).

            classroot.shown = true

            classroot.idle = false
            setTimeout(() => { if (classroot.gen == g2) classroot.idle = true }, 1000)
            }

    // the travel: underdamped springs = motion toward the target + a little
    // arrival overshoot — the 3.4 bounce, by physics. The radius travels too:
    // the terminus reshapes to the control it surrounds.

    Spring [ attribute = x,      to = { classroot.tx }, stiffness = 220, damping = 16 ],
    Spring [ attribute = y,      to = { classroot.ty }, stiffness = 220, damping = 16 ],
    Spring [ attribute = width,  to = { classroot.tw }, stiffness = 220, damping = 18 ],
    Spring [ attribute = height, to = { classroot.th }, stiffness = 220, damping = 18 ],
    Spring [ attribute = rad,    to = { classroot.trad }, stiffness = 220, damping = 20 ],

    Spring [ attribute = opacity, to = { classroot.shown && !classroot.idle ? 0.9 : 0 }, stiffness = 90, damping = 20 ],

    // either, which is what pointerEvents (unlike a hit-test override) governs

    pointerEvents = "none",

    // the shape-hugging outline — a rounded rect at the sprung radius, drawn,
    // so it re-derives as the radius travels between silhouettes

    // the OL brackets and the shape-hugging outline are ONE rendition at two
    // coverages: four corner-anchored strokes whose straight arms extend
    // toward each edge's midpoint by cov ∈ (0..1]. cov = 1 → arms meet, a
    // closed outline; cov low → open corner brackets ("target sights").
    // Coverage is a pure function of DISTANCE from target, so the physics
    // does the choreography: a flight breaks the ring open mid-air and the
    // settle closes the sights around the new silhouette. Small targets skip
    // the bracket phase (a ring around a radio dot has no arms to open).

    draw(d: Draw) {
        const w = this.width, h = this.height
        const Q = Math.PI / 2
        const dist = Math.abs(this.x - this.tx) + Math.abs(this.y - this.ty) + Math.abs(this.width - this.tw) + Math.abs(this.height - this.th)
        const small = Math.min(w, h) < 40
        // Ruled 2026-07-17: the ring travels as a CLOSED outline, source shape
        // to destination shape — no bracket mode intervening. The sights
        // rendition survives behind `theme.focusSights = true` (data, not a
        // code path) for its possible return: fully open in motion, arms
        // sweeping shut inside the last 16px of settle.
        const cov = this.theme.focusSights == true && !small ? Math.max(0.22, 1 - dist / 16) : 1
        const lw = typeof this.theme.focusRingWidth == "number" ? this.theme.focusRingWidth : 3
        // The indicator is ONE band or TWO, by data: `focusRingInnerWidth` > 0
        // adds an inner stroke between the control and the outer one — the
        // Fluent (Redmond) two-tone focus rectangle, black over white. Both
        // passes are the same outline at different insets; the flight, the
        // sights, and the silhouette machinery are shared, not forked.
        const iw = typeof this.theme.focusRingInnerWidth == "number" ? this.theme.focusRingInnerWidth : 0
        const pass = (ins, lwp, color) => {
            const r = Math.max(1, Math.min(this.rad - ins, Math.min(w, h) / 2 - ins))
            const ax = Math.max(0, ((w - 2 * ins) / 2 - r) * cov)      // horizontal arm length
            const ay = Math.max(0, ((h - 2 * ins) / 2 - r) * cov)      // vertical arm length
            d.strokeStyle = color
            d.lineWidth = lwp
            d.beginPath()
            // each corner: arc + arms, inset symmetrically
            d.moveTo(ins + r + ax, ins); d.lineTo(ins + r, ins); d.arc(ins + r, ins + r, r, -Q, Math.PI, true); d.lineTo(ins, ins + r + ay)
            d.moveTo(w - ins - r - ax, ins); d.lineTo(w - ins - r, ins); d.arc(w - ins - r, ins + r, r, -Q, 0); d.lineTo(w - ins, ins + r + ay)
            d.moveTo(w - ins, h - ins - r - ay); d.lineTo(w - ins, h - ins - r); d.arc(w - ins - r, h - ins - r, r, 0, Q); d.lineTo(w - ins - r - ax, h - ins)
            d.moveTo(ins + r + ax, h - ins); d.lineTo(ins + r, h - ins); d.arc(ins + r, h - ins - r, r, Q, Math.PI); d.lineTo(ins, h - ins - r - ay)
            d.stroke()
            }
        pass(0, lw, typeof this.theme.focusColor == "number" ? this.theme.focusColor : this.theme.accent)
        if (iw > 0) pass((lw + iw) / 2, iw, typeof this.theme.focusRingInnerColor == "number" ? this.theme.focusRingInnerColor : this.theme.surface)
        }
    ]

/*
# The Desktop

A Mac-style desktop, declared — windows, a dock, menus, and an embedded
app, the whole thing built from shapes, gradients, and constraints with
no image assets to load. It is the library's widest proof: dozens of
independent relationships — which window is front, how far the dock has
swelled, what the menu bar belongs to — all held true at once by the
runtime while you drag, resize, zoom, and click.

- **Windows** are their own layer, created at runtime by name. One
  `Window` class carries the chrome — a title bar you drag, edges and
  corners you resize (each with its resize cursor), a shadow that deepens
  when the window is front, and close / minimize / zoom controls — and
  subclasses carry the contents.
- **Files** browses this repository's own documentation, its column tree
  derived live from the docs model. **Viewer** renders any of those
  documents. **AppWindow** hosts a whole other Declare program as an
  embedded child — the dock's Calendar opens the real calendar app.
- The **dock** magnifies by layout, not paint: each icon's width is a
  constraint over its resting center, so neighbors displace and the
  plate stretches to hold them. Minimized windows park here as live
  thumbnails, riding the same swell and wearing their app's icon.
- The **menu bar** is whole menus expressed as records, and it follows
  focus — the menus belong to the front window's application, with a
  brand mark in the leading slot, a live Window menu, and a Help menu
  whose search field is a real text input. Keyboard shortcuts dispatch
  from the same records the bar is drawn from.

Every icon, control, and texture is drawn from shapes and gradients, so
the desktop carries no image payload at all — pure description. (The one
bitmap is a certain music-video still, and it earns its keep.)
*/

// The window classes below are created only at runtime, by name — a window
// RECORD carries its class as a string, and WinSlot (the replication hinge)
// creates it — never as a declared tag. Class reachability is otherwise a
// static fact (unused classes are dropped, which is what tree-shakes
// production builds), and a name inside a runtime string is invisible to that
// analysis. `use` is the explicit bridge: keep these classes registered for
// creation by name.

use [ BracketIcon, CodeIcon, AutoIcon, LightbulbIcon, FilesWindow, ViewerWindow, AppWindow, AboutWindow, JotWindow, BrandMark, HelpSearch, AppGlyph, CautionBadge ]

/*
## Window — chrome once, contents per subclass

Every window on the desktop is one of these. `Window` carries all of the
chrome — the shadow, the resize edges and corners, and the shade / zoom /
minimize behaviors — and each subclass (Files, Viewer, AppWindow, About,
Jot) supplies only its contents. Geometry the class shares is named
once (`barH`, `minW`, `gutter`, `corner`…) so no derived position below
carries a bare number.

Two motions drive most of the class. **Open and close** run `baseScale`
from the icon a window launched from up to full size and back, so it grows
out of its dock icon and shrinks into it. **Minimize** doesn't hide a
window — it parks it in the dock as a live thumbnail that rides the same
magnification swell as the icons, blended by `miniT` from a free window
(0) to a docked one (1).

    inkHi: Color = #0000006B,                    // front-window shadow ink

    // ("" = nothing open). Every level of the hierarchy — even the top — is DATA
    // (app.docsModel.value.browse, the one documentation model); this window
    // chooses no categories of its own.

    rootPath: string = "",                       // the folder this window is ROOTED at ("" = the whole tree); a double-clicked folder opens a new window rooted at itself

    cw0: number = 0,                             // divider-drag anchors
    cpx0: number = 0,
    cwk: number = -1,                            // depth of the column being dragged

    pendingItem: object,                         // that item's record (name/path/doc/hasKids/at) — what a second click opens
    pendingPX: number = 0,                       // the pointer at the first click (root space) — a double-click is
    pendingPY: number = 0,                       //   time + POINTER distance, so a row sliding under the cursor

    // it — so a row's click is one assignment and truncation is automatic (the
    // list re-derives). Miller columns fall straight out of a recursive walk.

    columnData(selPath: string, model: object, rootPath: string) -> array {
        const rootParts = rootPath == "" ? [] : rootPath.split("\n")
        const parts = selPath == "" ? [] : selPath.split("\n")

        const drill = parts.slice(rootParts.length)
        const cols = []

        for (let k = 0; k < drill.length; k = k + 1) {
            const chosen = level.find((n) => n.name == drill[k])

            const prefix = rootParts.concat(drill.slice(0, k + 1))

reactive graph, input router, sized to the island's box. The path is relative,
so `"../../calendar/calendar"` reaches the real calendar app: no copy, no shim.

child's own name, `island.childName`), activation, and the `dark` + `extraEnv`
environment it hands the island.

    // child (`island.childName`): the viewer titles by the file it shows and
    // follows its navigation. `appTitle` is the fallback until the child is up.

    appTitle: string = "",
    title = { this.island.childName != "" ? this.island.childName : this.appTitle },

    // the slot's ENV segment (after `|`) is the embedding environment — the
    // host parses it into the child's reactive `app.env`, at mount and on
    // every change: toggling the desktop's appearance re-marks the slot and
    // the hosted app re-derives (its Auto mode follows `app.env.dark`)

    // a press anywhere in the hosted app also lands here (the router remaps
    // embedded presses to the island — dom-backend), so clicking the child's
    // content raises this window exactly as clicking any window body does

    island: AppIsland [ x = 0, y = { classroot.barH }, width = { parent.width }, height = { parent.height - classroot.barH },

        // declares `external darkOverride: string` gets this as a checked
        // fact, handshake and all. TRI-STATE by sentinel — "dark" / "light",
        // "" = the host has no opinion (an unlinked tenant's default, so its
        // Auto mode falls through to its own app.dark). The desktop always
        // has an opinion. `env.dark` below stays — the untyped ancestor — so
        // every existing tenant keeps working; new tenants should pair.

        external darkOverride: string = { this.root.darkMode ? "dark" : "light" },

        pad: View [ x = 48, y = 40, width = { parent.width - 96 },

                visible = { classroot.inlineDoc == "" && classroot.src.loading }, text = "Loading…" ],
            failed: Text [ fontSize = 13, textColor = { this.theme.textFaint }, wrap = true, width = { parent.width },
                visible = { classroot.inlineDoc == "" && classroot.src.failed },
                text = { "Could not load — " + (classroot.src.error || "") } ],
            doc: Markdown [ width = { parent.width },
                visible = { classroot.inlineDoc != "" || classroot.src.loaded },
                richTextLayout = { { default: { maxWidth: 560 }, code: { maxWidth: 0 } } },

                codeBackground = { this.root.darkMode ? 0x35393F : 0xE9EFF4 },
                codeRule = { this.root.darkMode ? 0x37E0C8 : 0x12A08D },
                dark = { this.root.darkMode },
                text = { classroot.inlineDoc != "" ? classroot.inlineDoc : (classroot.src.value || "") } ]

## JotWindow — a sticky note with its own chrome

A custom window type: square corners, yellow paper, and — when active — a
saturated title strip carrying olive-outlined pale widgets (a close box at the
left; a zoom triangle and a collapse box at the right). An inactive note is
chromeless: the strip and widgets vanish into the paper. It keeps all of the
base `Window`'s behavior — drag, the activation shadow, shade, resize edges —
through `chrome = false`, so here chrome is a skin, not the skeleton.
*/

    title = "",                                  // untitled — labels fall back to the app's name
    note: string = "",                           // the note's seed text

    // linework #DBC501 dark olive over #FFF49C pale, and a half-pixel
    // #4E4E52 rim — a full CSS pixel reads as drawn-on lines, not an edge

    fill = #FEF49C,
    stroke = { stroke(0.5, 0x4E4E52) },
    inkHi = #00000052,
    inkLo = #00000038,
    shadow = { this.root.wm.frontWin == this ? shadow(0, 10, 26, this.inkHi) : shadow(0, 3, 9, this.inkLo) },

    strip: View [ x = 0, y = 0, width = { parent.width }, height = { classroot.barH },
        fill = { classroot.active ? 0xFEEA3D : 0xFEF49C },
        onPointerDown() { classroot.beginDrag() },
        onPointerMove() { classroot.dragTo() },
        onPointerUp(e: PointerUpEvent)   { classroot.endDrag(e.canceled) },
        onHold() { classroot.activate() },   // the hold rider — same claim shape as the title bar; it also raises

        // the strip's widgets: dark olive outlines around pale interiors —
        // the close box 11px in from the left, the zoom triangle (right
        // angle at bottom-right) and the collapse box in from the right

        closeBox: View [ visible = { classroot.active }, x = 11, y = 2.25, width = 7.5, height = 7.5,

            onClick() { this.root.wm.closeWin(classroot) }
            ],
        zoomW: View [ visible = { classroot.active }, x = { parent.width - 33 }, y = 2.25, width = 8, height = 8,
            onClick() { classroot.zoomToggle() },
            draw(d: Draw) {
                d.fillStyle = 0xFFF49C
                d.strokeStyle = 0xDBC501
                d.lineWidth = 1.4
                d.beginPath()
                d.moveTo(0.7, 7.3); d.lineTo(7.3, 7.3); d.lineTo(7.3, 0.7)

                d.fillRect(0.7, 0.7, 6.6, 6.6)
                d.strokeStyle = 0xDBC501
                d.lineWidth = 1.4

                d.stroke()
                d.beginPath()

                d.stroke()
                }
            ]

    // the note body is formatted — a Markdown field on the paper (no input
    // chrome, no focus ring; the note's text is authored, not typed)

    pad: View [ x = 12, y = { classroot.barH + 6 }, clip = true,
        width = { parent.width - 24 }, height = { parent.height - classroot.barH - 16 },
        md: Markdown [ width = { parent.width }, dark = false,
            bodyColor = 0x1D1D1F, scale = 0.82, lineHeight = 1.45,

/*
## MiniTile — a minimized window's dock tile

An invisible click target that rides the same magnification swell as the
icons, so its hit area and label track the live thumbnail beneath it (the
thumbnail is the parked window itself). The tile sits in the dock layer above
the parked window, so a click restores it instead of poking its tiny content.
Its pill is the `DockIcon`'s, showing the window's title.
*/

class MiniTile extends View [

    // REPLICATED over the WM's parked records (wm.miniData, one tile per
    // record, keyed by the window's id) — the static six-slot pool this
    // replaced existed only because per-row liveness couldn't then be
    // trusted; the records era ends with the cap

    ix: number = { Number(this.$data(["ix"]) ?? 0) },
    recId: string = { "" + (this.$data(["id"]) ?? "") },
    lbl: string = { "" + (this.$data(["label"]) ?? "") },
    appId: string = { "" + (this.$data(["appId"]) ?? "") },

    // geometry straight from the mini layout (the same entries the parked
    // window reads), translated into the minis section's local space

    slotW: number = { this.root.dock.miniLayout != null && this.ix < this.root.dock.miniLayout.length ? this.root.dock.miniLayout[this.ix].w : 48 },
    slotH: number = { this.root.dock.miniLayout != null && this.ix < this.root.dock.miniLayout.length ? this.root.dock.miniLayout[this.ix].h : 48 },
    slotRestW: number = { this.root.dock.miniLayout != null && this.ix < this.root.dock.miniLayout.length ? this.root.dock.miniLayout[this.ix].rw : 48 },
    waveMag: number = { this.slotW / Math.max(1, this.slotRestW) },
    x = { (this.root.dock.miniLayout != null && this.ix < this.root.dock.miniLayout.length ? this.root.dock.miniLayout[this.ix].x : 0) - (this.root.dock.x + this.root.dock.row.width + 32) },
    width = { this.slotW },
    height = { this.slotH },   // the thumbnail's aspect height (not icon-square), so the badge lands on the thumbnail's own corner
    y = { parent.height - 13.5 - 30.5 * this.waveMag - this.height / 2 },   // scales around the badge baseline (grows upward on rollover); at rest this is the plate center
    onClick() { this.root.wm.restoreMiniAt(this.ix) },

    // the app-icon badge — on the tile (the dock layer, above the plate's
    // frost, so it renders crisp), gated by geometry: it shows exactly while
    // the window is seated in this slot — its visual width equals the slot's
    // (both sides derive from the same layout entry, so the equality holds
    // through the magnification wave, and never mid-journey: a traveling or
    // restored window's scale·width can't match). Pure derived fact, read
    // LIVE off the window itself — no journey bookkeeping.

    seated: boolean = { this.root.wm.seated(this.recId, this.slotW) },

    // The badge is the app's own dock icon at badge scale — same class, same
    // art, so the calendar badge carries the live date.
    // Its wave/size/position constraints are displaced at this use site, and
    // its pointer handlers forward to the tile (so no second pill appears).

    badge: DockIcon [
        visible = { classroot.seated },
        width = { this.root.dock.badgeEdge * classroot.waveMag }, height = { this.root.dock.badgeEdge * classroot.waveMag },

        // x tracks the thumbnail's right edge (2px inside it); y sits on the
        // dock's common badge baseline (13.5px above the plate floor), not the
        // thumbnail's own bottom — so a short or landscape thumbnail's badge
        // hangs below it while a tall one stays contained. The tile's center is
        // the plate center; baseline = center + (44 - 13.5).

        x = { parent.width - (this.root.dock.badgeEdge + 2) * classroot.waveMag },
        y = { parent.height / 2 + (30.5 - this.root.dock.badgeEdge) * classroot.waveMag },
        appId = { classroot.appId },
        onClick() { this.root.wm.restoreMiniAt(classroot.ix) }
        ],

    // the label pill — the DockIcon's, verbatim geometry: it floats just above
    // the tile's OWN top (local y), tail tip meeting it, so it rides the
    // magnified crest exactly as the app-icon pill does

    pill: View [ visible = { classroot.hovered },   // the TILE's hover, not the pill's:
        //  a pill hidden until hovered could never show itself (an invisible view
        //  is not on the hit chain), so the fact has to come from what it labels

        width = { this.t.width + 26 }, height = 33,
        x = center,
        y = { parent.height / 2 - 102 },   // pinned to the shared pill baseline (~62px above the plate top), same Y as the app-icon pills
        bodyH: number = 22,
        draw(d: Draw) { this.root.drawPill(d, this.width, this.bodyH, this.root.darkMode) },
        t: Text [ x = center, y = { (this.parent.bodyH - this.height) / 2 }, fontSize = 13,
            textColor = { this.root.darkMode ? 0xF2F2F5 : 0x1D1D1F },
            text = { classroot.lbl } ]
        ]
    ]


/*
## DockIcon — a drawn, labeled icon that magnifies by layout

Each icon's live width springs toward a target read from the pointer's distance
to its resting center, so hovering the dock swells the icons under the pointer
and displaces their neighbors. The magnification is layout, not paint: the
widths really change and the plate stretches to hold them.
*/

class DockIcon extends View [

    // per-icon inputs, fed at the use site

    ix: number = 0,                              // resting slot index
    slots: number = { this.root.launcher.roster.length },   // total icons — derived from the catalog

    // THE application — an L-20 POINTER SLOT: the { } computes which launcher
    // instance this icon is (a reference; re-pointing when the id moves — a
    // MiniTile badge's does — and owning nothing). Face, hues, dot, pill, and
    // the click all read the one instance THROUGH the slot; those reads ride
    // the tracking path, so they stay live on whichever node it points at.

    appId: string = "",
    ap: DesktopApp = { this.root.launcher.byId(this.appId) ?? this.root.launcher.files },   // total: the transient first-settle read (a replicated row before its id lands) falls to Files instead of throwing
    running: boolean = false,                    // fed from the data row at the use site (the live flag rides the records)

    // shared geometry — one place for the numbers the constraints below share

    rest: number = { this.root.dock.iconEdge },             // resting icon size (the shared cell)
    pitch: number = { this.root.dock.iconEdge + 16 },       // slot-center spacing: the resting size plus a 16px gap
    strip: number = 16,                          // the running-dot band below the icons

    // the face is rendered ONCE at this fixed reference size and paint-scaled to
    // the live magnified width (the plate's `scale` below). It must be ≥ the
    // largest magnified size (rest · 1.55 ≈ 87pt) so the transform only ever
    // DOWNsamples the hi-res raster — smooth, no shimmer — while the illustration
    // and rim draw()s invalidate only on real content change (calendar day,
    // theme), never per magnification frame. This keeps the wave inside Safari's
    // frame budget: 9 GPU blits, not 9 vector re-rasters, every frame.

    face: number = 96,

    // the resting slot center in app coords — the magnification's source must
    // not read the magnified layout (a feedback loop); resting geometry is
    // fixed: `pitch` about the app's center

    cx0: number = { this.root.width / 2 + (this.ix - (this.slots - 1) / 2) * this.pitch - this.root.dock.miniSpan / 2 },

    // magnification: the shared wave (app.dockMag) about my resting center,
    // read off the SMOOTHED pointer (dockX) so it glides every frame, and
    // scaled by the enter/exit envelope (the dock's `hot`) so entering and
    // leaving glide too. Neighbors displace as the widths change — the wave
    // is layout, not paint.

    // Each icon springs its OWN magnification toward a target read from the raw
    // pointer, so every icon is always mid-flight during motion and the swell
    // glides continuously — smoother than a single shared spring, which would
    // settle between the browser's coalesced pointer events and step. The
    // resting center (cx0) feeds the distance, so the swell never reads its own
    // magnified output.

    // The dock's enter/exit gate, DECLARED rather than groped for. This class
    // is hosted in two places — the dock row (which feeds the dock's live
    // gate at the instance) and a MiniTile badge (which feeds nothing) — and
    // the default 0 IS the badge's contract: a host that states no gate is a
    // host with no wave, so the badge's spring parks at 1. The old shape
    // reached this.parent.parent.hotGate and coped with `undefined` at run
    // time; that once fed six springs a NaN target they chased for the life
    // of the session (F1) — a typed slot with a stated default cannot.

    hotGate: number = 0,

    magTarget: number = { 1 + (this.root.dock.dockMag(this.root.pointerX - this.cx0) - 1) * this.hotGate },
    mag: number = 1,
    magSpring: Spring [ attribute = mag, to = { classroot.magTarget }, stiffness = 1300, damping = 62, epsilon = 0.002 ],
    width  = { this.rest * this.mag },
    height = { this.width },
    y = { parent.height - this.height - this.strip - this.hopY },   // bottom-anchored above the dot strip

    // The launch bounce: a ballistic arc — decelerating up, gravity down —
    // twice, about 560ms per bounce, poked by the app when an application first
    // opens (or first opens again after a Quit). The group cascades `attribute`
    // to its members; each leg is one half of the parabola.

    hopY: number = 0,

    bounce: AnimatorGroup [ attribute = hopY, process = sequential,
        Animator [ to = 30, duration = 300, motion = quadOut ],
        Animator [ to = 0, duration = 260, motion = quadIn ],
        Animator [ to = 30, duration = 300, motion = quadOut ],
        Animator [ to = 0, duration = 260, motion = quadIn ]
        ],

    poke() { this.bounce.start() },
    plate: View [ x = 0, y = 0, width = { classroot.face }, height = { classroot.face },
        // Paint-only magnification: the face is drawn once at `face`px and the
        // GPU scales it (about the top-left, so it fills the bottom-anchored box)
        // to the live width — no per-frame re-raster of the illustration or rim.
        // The DockIcon's LAYOUT width still grows, so neighbors displace as
        // before: the swell stays layout; only each icon's paint is cached.

        scale = { classroot.width / classroot.face },
        cornerRadius = { this.width * 0.23 }, clip = true,
        fill = { gradient(classroot.ap.hue1, classroot.ap.hue2) },

        // Glyph sizes stay fractional — rounding them would tick the art in
        // whole-pixel steps while the plate glides subpixel, a visible jitter.

        g: Text [ x = center, y = center, fontWeight = semibold, textColor = 0xFFFFFF,
            fontSize = { this.parent.width * classroot.ap.gsize },
            visible = { !classroot.ap.drawn && classroot.ap.glyph != "" },
            text = { classroot.ap.glyph } ],

        // Drawn app art, authored in a 48-unit box and scaled to fill the plate.

        art: View [ x = 0, y = 0, width = { parent.width }, height = { parent.height },
            visible = { classroot.ap.drawn },

            // the illustration is drawn at the icon's LIVE size — a canvas
            // scale inside draw() (vector, recomputed every frame) rather than
            // a CSS transform stretching a fixed 48px raster, which re-samples
            // and jitters a pixel as the magnification glides. The app's face
            // keeps its 48-unit authoring coordinates; only the scale moved
            // inward. (The calendar's live weekday + day are part of ITS face,
            // so the whole mark scales as one unit and re-records on the flip.)

            draw(d: Draw) {
                d.scale(this.width / 48, this.width / 48)
                const a = classroot.ap
                if (a != null) a.face(d)
                }
            ],

        // The icon's glossy edge — the same top-lit rim the dock plate carries,
        // scaled to the icon and drawn at its live size (no raster jitter as it
        // magnifies). A 1px white highlight, brightest along the top and fading
        // down, like the sheen a glossy rounded tile catches from above.

        rim: View [ x = 0, y = 0, width = { parent.width }, height = { parent.height },
            draw(d: Draw) {
                const w = this.width
                const h = this.height
                if (w < 3 || h < 3) return       // a freshly replicated tile's first paint can be 0×0 — nothing to rim
                const r = w * 0.23
                const g = d.createLinearGradient(0, 0, 0, h)
                g.addColorStop(0, "rgba(255,255,255,0.42)")
                g.addColorStop(0.34, "rgba(255,255,255,0.07)")
                g.addColorStop(1, "rgba(255,255,255,0)")
                d.strokeStyle = g
                d.lineWidth = 1
                d.beginPath()
                d.roundRect(0.5, 0.5, w - 1, h - 1, r - 0.5)
                d.stroke()
                }
            ]
        ],

    // the running-app dot, centered in the strip below the icon

    // the dot marks is-running and never bounces: adding hopY back cancels the
    // icon's launch-bounce offset, pinning the dot to the strip. MEASURED from
    // the running dot: near-black on the light shelf, ~4px across — not muted
    // gray. theme.text IS that value (0x1D1D1F light) and flips to a light dot
    // under a dark theme, so it always reads against the shelf.

    dot: View [ width = 4, height = 4, cornerRadius = 2,
        x = { (parent.width - 4) / 2 }, y = { parent.height + 6 + this.parent.hopY },
        visible = { classroot.running }, fill = { this.theme.text } ],

    // The label pill — the dock's own tooltip: a frosted chip with a downward
    // pointer tick and no shadow. It floats just above the hovered icon's own
    // top, so its tail tip meets the icon and — since the hovered icon is the
    // swell's peak — it clears every neighbor. As the icon magnifies and its top
    // rises, the pill rides up with it.

    pill: View [ visible = { classroot.hovered },   // the ICON's hover, not the pill's
        width = { this.t.width + 26 }, height = 33,
        x = center,
        y = { parent.height - 130 },   // pinned to the shared pill baseline, so it lands right at any magnification
        bodyH: number = 22,
        draw(d: Draw) { this.root.drawPill(d, this.width, this.bodyH, this.root.darkMode) },
        t: Text [ x = center, y = { (this.parent.bodyH - this.height) / 2 }, fontSize = 13,
            textColor = { this.root.darkMode ? 0xF2F2F5 : 0x1D1D1F },
            text = { classroot.ap.label } ]
        ]
    ]


/*
### The clock

Today, as a fact: the menu bar's live readout, the calendar dock icon's date
face, and an About window's date all read the same node. Self-driving — it
arms its own 15-second timer at init, so no host wiring exists to forget.
*/

class DesktopClock extends Time [ tick = minute,
    // Numbers in, this desktop's words out: the facts are Time's, the format is
    // the app's. `minute` is the resolution both readouts need, so the menu bar
    // and the calendar icon flip together, on the minute — aligned, drift-free,
    // and paused by itself on a page nobody can see.

    text: string = { ["Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun"][this.weekday - 1] + " " + ["Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun", "Jul", "Aug", "Sep", "Oct", "Nov", "Dec"][this.month - 1] + " " + this.day + "  " + (this.hour % 12 == 0 ? 12 : this.hour % 12) + ":" + (this.minute < 10 ? "0" : "") + this.minute + " " + (this.hour >= 12 ? "PM" : "AM") },
    dayName: string = { ["MON", "TUE", "WED", "THU", "FRI", "SAT", "SUN"][this.weekday - 1] },
    dayNum: number = { this.day }
    ]


/*
### The applications

An APPLICATION is a node: one instance per app the desktop offers, declared
under the launcher and reachable by name (`app.launcher.calendar`). The
instance carries everything that is the app's own — identity (label, title,
blurb), the icon (plate hues, a text glyph or a drawn `face`), launch state
(`running`/`launching`/`count`, plain reactive attributes — assignment is the
update, no record ceremony), policy (`alwaysRunning`, `canOpen`, `place`),
and the `launch` verb behind its dock icon and menu items. (The verb was
renamed from `open` when the extractor's old by-name call resolution collided
it with the library combobox's `open()` — the phantom-".start()" trap this
file hit twice. That resolution is gone: since L-21 (2026-09-01) calls
resolve with TS semantics through the typecheck's own checker, so the name is
free again; `launch` stays because it is the better verb for a dock icon.)

One taxonomy covers every citizen. A BUILT-IN app (Files, Jots) opens windows
of this very program. A HOSTED app (Calendar, 50 Birds, Declare Viewer) is a
FOREIGN program carried the same way — hosting is a subclass with a program
path, not a different mechanism. An INERT app (Write, Mail, Music, Terminal)
owns a quip and raises the alert. Chrome never switches on an app id: the
dock icon, the About box, the alert sheet, and a minimized window's badge all
read the ONE instance, so the art, the name, and the running dot cannot
disagree — and adding an application is one class plus one roster entry.

`face(d)` is the icon's art, authored in the dock's 48-unit box; the caller
scales first and has painted the plate hue behind (AppGlyph, DockIcon). It is
a method, so a face that reads live state — the calendar's date — re-records
when that state changes, like any tracked drawing.
*/

class DesktopApp extends Node [
    id: string = "",
    label: string = "",                          // the dock pill's short name
    title: string = "",                          // the formal name — menus, About
    blurb: string = "",                          // the About box's line
    glyph: string = "",                          // a text-glyph mark (M↓, ♪, [ ]) …
    gsize: number = 0.42,                        //   … at this fraction of the plate
    drawn: boolean = false,                      // … or a drawn face() — this flag picks
    hue1: Color = #4A90D9,                       // plate gradient, top → bottom
    hue2: Color = #2E5FA3,
    src: string = "desktop.declare",             // View & Edit Source's subject
    quip: string = "",                           // an inert app's refusal
    running: boolean = false,
    launching: boolean = false,                  // mid launch-bounce (guards a double-click)
    count: number = 0,                           // open windows (informational)
    alwaysRunning: boolean = false,              // Files: no Quit item
    canOpen: boolean = true,                     // calendar: Open… disabled
    face(d: Draw) { },                           // drawn icon art, in the 48-unit box
    launch(v: View?) { }                         // what New and a dock click do
    ]


class HostedApp extends DesktopApp [             // a foreign program — the same citizen
    prog: string = "",                           // the program the window's island mounts
    env: string = "",                            // its embedding environment segment
    place: string = "",                          // window placement policy ("clearDock")
    launch(v: View?) { this.root.launcher.openHosted(this, v, "") }
